explanation: RAII is a C++ programming idiom where resource acquisition (such as file handles, memory, or network connections) is tied to object lifetime. When an object is created, it acquires resources, and when it is destroyed (goes out of scope), it releases those resources automatically. This pattern ensures exception-safe resource management, preventing leaks and ensuring proper cleanup even in error conditions. In the context of C++, RAII is fundamental for managing resources like file streams, memory, and locks, leveraging constructors and destructors to automate cleanup.
